**Triage — `domain:cli` confirmed.** `tooling` · `i18n` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` kept. Read 2026-09-04T06:39Z.

You asked triage to *"confirm `domain:cli` rather than re-deriving the routing from the title"* — confirmed, and derived from the **landing point**, not the title and not the ruling's wording: the emitter goes in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts`, and `packages/cli` is the first entry in the lane table's `domain:cli` row. The ruling's named destination and the landing-point test agree, which is the reassuring case.

⚠️ **Your routing note was right, and the sweep branch it names did not fire.** This card sat **19.5 h** carrying `tooling` · `priority:p2` · `i18n` and no `domain:*` — everything except the one label that makes it visible. That is this seat's miss, not queue age; I measured the class last round and it was **29** such cards in this repo, all of them recent. Yours is one of the ones I am now working through.

⭐ Worth flagging what made this instance more expensive than a normal routing gap: **the dependency runs backwards here.** PR #14763 stays `draft` until this emitter is on `main`, so an unrouted card was holding a *different lane's* gate out of the queue. A card nobody can see is bad; a card nobody can see that another lane is waiting on is a stall with no visible cause on either side.

## ⛔ What triage is not deciding

- ⛔ Not re-opening the #14653 ruling. `settings` gets a real emitter; `messages` / `settingsCommon` stay the ledger's two authorised entries; **no third ledger entry as a bridge**, as the ruling forbids explicitly.
- ⛔ Not the exemption ledger or `LEDGER_CEILING` — devx's half, on PR #14763's branch.
- ⛔ p2 left as filed. It gates another lane's PR, which argues upward, but the filing seat priced it and nothing measured here contradicts that.

Same-batch siblings: #14241 (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/**`, possibly a new `packages/cli` test file — different file, same package is EXEMPT under seat ruling ①) and #14849 (`packages/rest/src/*.test.ts`). In-flight PR #15304 is `packages/runtime` + one `packages/spec` line; PR #15300 is in the merge queue on `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` + three others — ⛔ **neither touches `src/utils/`**. ⚠️ Read coupling: **#14728 is deliberately left in the queue** — it is about `check:i18n-coverage` miscounting, and this card changes what the extractor emits, so dispatching both at once would have each moving the other's numbers.

### The ruling is the spec here, and it is quoted rather than paraphrased

The maintainer adopted **option A** on #14653 (director seat, summon #11, ruling comment `5522887332`; maintainer's verbatim reply 「同意」), and the ruled shape is quoted on this card's body verbatim — read it there. The operative sentence: `settings` is **walked** by a registry-driven, config-independent emitter over the settings manifests, on the `walkMetadataForms` precedent, and **the fixture needs no change because the registry supplies the population**.

⛔ **Do not reach green by inventing key populations** — that is option C, and the ruling rejected it as widening the walker's contract.
⛔ **Do not add a third entry to the exemption ledger as a bridge** — the ruling forbids it explicitly. `messages` and `settingsCommon` stay as its two authorised entries.

### Executable acceptance criterion, given by the card

`node scripts/check-i18n-walk-parity.mjs` no longer reports `settings` among the declared-but-unwalked groups, with `messages` / `settingsCommon` still the only two ledger entries. ⚠️ That gate lives on **PR #14763's branch**, not on `main` — so verify the criterion against that branch's script, and ⛔ do not edit the script to make it pass.

### Sequencing runs the OTHER way — this card is in front

Per the ruling, **PR #14763 stays `draft` until this emitter is on `main`.** Devx is waiting on this, not the reverse, which is why the card carries no `Blocked-by:`. ⇒ Landing this unblocks another lane's gate; it is worth the care but ⛔ not worth widening scope to "help".

### Premise to re-derive

The card's measured basis is that `settings` is keyed by `SettingsManifest.namespace`, that the manifests are platform code under `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/` with an aggregate export in the directory index, and that `collectExpectedEntries` **already** enumerates `metadataForms` unconditionally via `walkMetadataForms` — the precedent to copy, in the same function. ⚠️ Verify all three on your own tree; anchors and exports move.

## Closed `not_planned` — this card executes a SUPERSEDED ruling. And the dispatch that sent a dev at it was my error.

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), R69, session `session_01D47qPfEWVPmhguWgBZCi5N`. `pm:dispatched` stripped, assignee cleared, card closed. ⛔ Nothing was implemented; no PR; no file in the shared checkout was touched.

### The provenance, verified by me on GitHub and on the tree — ⛔ not taken from the dev's report

| fact | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the ruling this card cites | #14653 `5522887332`, **2026-09-03T08:29Z** — option A of *that* round: `settings` gets a registry-driven emitter |
| the ruling that **supersedes** it | #14653 **`5535827386`, 2026-09-04T04:52:20Z** — director seat, summon 13. Maintainer verbatim (⛔ 照抄不译): 「按照你的建议，跟进并处理完这两个pr。」 |
| what it ruled | **A: all three unwalked groups enter the exemption ledger**, `LEDGER_CEILING` 0 → 3. It states in as many words: **⛔ "No emitter is built in this PR; `packages/cli/**` stays untouched"** |
| what it re-evaluated | exactly two options — A (ledger all three now, finding for `settings`) and **B (ledger two and build a `settings` emitter FIRST)**. ⭐ **B is precisely what this card embodies, and the maintainer declined it** |
| where the terminal state now lives | finding **#15178** (corrected from #15150 by `5535829928`) — emitter **or** removal from the per-app schema under ADR-0049, explicitly *"a deferral, not a fact"* |
| and it already LANDED | PR #14763 is on `origin/main` as **`9c1bcda3`**, merged 05:52:47Z — **5h43m before I dispatched** |

⇒ This card's entire sequencing rationale — *"PR #14763 stays draft until this emitter is on main; devx is waiting on this card"* — is **inverted on the tree**. Devx landed green **without** the emitter. Two further premises in my dispatch fall with it: the gate is on `main` and wired (`package.json`, `lint.yml`), not on a branch; and the ledger holds **three** entries at `LEDGER_CEILING 3`, not the two my brief called its "only two authorised entries".

### ⛔ Building the emitter now would REDDEN a currently-green gate

The dev measured this rather than predicting it, using the shipped gate's own exported classifier and ⛔ without editing the gate: today `parityVerdict` reports `unwalked []`, `staleWalked []`. Add `settings` to the walked set — this card's change — and it becomes `staleWalked: ['settings']`, `reportStale` fires *"the walker DOES emit it now; the exemption is spent"*, **exit 1**. The only remedy the gate names is deleting the ledger entry and ratcheting `LEDGER_CEILING` 3 → 2 — the maintainer-governed file my own brief forbade the dev to touch, twice.

So the acceptance criterion this card gives is **already satisfied on `main` with no emitter** (`11 declared group(s), 8 walked, 3 exempted — every declared group has an extractor face`, exit 0). There was nothing left for this card to buy.

### ⛔ My error, stated plainly

The decision re-read is mandatory before dispatch words are written, and it exists for exactly this: a ruling can be closed in the other direction between a card being filed and being picked up. I read this card's body — accurate when written at 2026-09-03T10:57Z — confirmed its three technical premises **on the tree**, and dispatched. I did **not** follow the ruling chain back to #14653 to ask whether `5522887332` was still the current ruling. It was not, and had not been for 18 hours.

⭐ The lane rule this earns: **a card that cites a ruling is citing a snapshot. Re-read the ruling AT ITS SOURCE before dispatch, not the card's quotation of it** — the card cannot update itself when the ruling moves, and a stale quotation reads exactly as authoritative as a live one.

### ⭐ The dev's census is the durable output, and it is going where it belongs

Asked for a `no-emitter` finding, it instead ran the measurement **#15178 itself asks for** and produced the answer: **zero per-app readers of the `settings` group.** By #15178's own stated rule (*"Zero per-app readers points at 2 (removal under ADR-0049); a per-app reader points at 1 (emitter)"*) that points at **removal** — i.e. away from this card. Posted to #15178 as its first grading input, where the decision actually lives.

### Why closed rather than held

`pm:on-hold` needs a machine-readable restart condition, and there is none: the terminal choice is genuinely undecided and is carried by an open `finding` that is explicitly **not** a queue card. This card has no independent future — if #15178 rules "emitter", the card for it gets filed then, against whatever the tree looks like at that point. Closing keeps the record and costs nothing: **reopening is free and the maintainer can veto this.**

### ⚠️ One leftover for a human

The zero-commit probe branch `claude/issue-14932-i18n-settings-registry-emitter` is on `origin` at `6e67b86c` (identical to `origin/main`, no commits). The dev's delete was refused by its container's command classifier — the known shape of #12771 (*agent seats cannot delete their own remote branches*). It needs deleting by hand.
